solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cryptic clue to "Uganda" is not classified

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure or puzzling, so the letters of the following words are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's hint for the country Uganda turns out to be unofficial or unlisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be describing a crossword clue for Uganda; in fact 'Cryptic' rearranges the twelve letters of CLUE TO UGANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncatalogued has not been entered in any list or sorted into a category.

clue.text: Lewd relative decapitated husband

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off the word

parts.note: a man is a husband, as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A dirty-minded family member beheaded her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean in a moral sense means impure or obscene, so it can describe lewd thoughts.

clue.text: Mass resistance led by church inspires passion

indicators.note: led by means the church comes ahead of the resistance letter
to inspire is to breathe in, so the church and resistance pieces take the passion inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
lust is strong passion
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Widespread opposition headed by the church stirs strong feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service, but it is a noun for a cluster.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster is a mass or bunch of things grouped closely together.

clue.text: Tedious work's introduction to tedious study on philosopher

indicators.note: introduction to means only the opening letter of tedious is used

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher

explanation.surface: Dull work begins with dull study of a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a monotonous routine, figuratively the same dreary round of toil every day.

clue.text: Generous drink? Bottom's up!

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom letter of the drink word rises higher, a play on the toast bottoms up

parts.note: lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A generous serving of booze, and a toast of cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom's up' is the drinker's toast, but here the bottom letter, R, of LAGER moves up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean generous or liberal, as in a large helping or a large-hearted gift.

clue.text: Hostile upper-class purged in Caligula's new order

indicators.note: a new order means the emperor's letters are rearranged once the upper-class letter is purged

parts.note: the name Caligula, the possessive ending being only the link

explanation.surface: A cold aristocracy is wiped out in a mad emperor's new regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purged in' removes U from CALIGULA, and 'new order' rearranges the remaining CALIGLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial manners are icily cold and unfriendly, so hostile in attitude.

clue.text: How English literature adopting elevated pose might be seen

definitions.text: How English literature adopting elevated pose might be seen

indicators.note: adopting means the literature word takes the turned pose inside
elevated, raised up in a down entry, means the word for pose is read upwards

parts.note: to sit is to pose, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: English literature putting on airs could be considered snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' means read upwards, which suits a down entry; 'adopting' signals the insertion. Read whole, the clue also says how lofty English literature might look.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours a select, superior few; literature that strikes a lofty pose would look snobbish.

clue.text: Proving blasé insight is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Showing that a jaded perception is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Establishing a fact is demonstrating it to be true beyond doubt.

clue.text: Shut off contact from witness charged by Conservative judge

indicators.note: to be charged by something is to be filled with it, so the witness word takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: to witness is to see
LUD is a form of lord, as in the courtroom address m'lud to a judge

explanation.surface: A witness is kept isolated after being charged with an offence by a Tory judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged by' looks like a criminal charge but means filled with. M'lud ('my lord') is how British barristers address a judge in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To seclude someone is to isolate them, keeping them away from company and dealings with others.

clue.text: Pragmatic view is taken in particular area

indicators.note: taken in means the word is is held inside the area word

parts.note: a realm is a particular field or domain

explanation.surface: A practical outlook is adopted within a specialist field.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is the attitude of accepting things as they really are and dealing with them practically.

clue.text: Governing body of international partner blocking opening of modern university and business centre

indicators.note: opening of means only the first letter of modern is wanted
blocking means the pieces obstruct the business centre by sitting inside it

parts.note: the City is London's financial and business district
a pal is a partner or mate

explanation.surface: A council of an overseas partner obstructs the founding of a new university and commercial hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' signals the insertion, made just after the first letter. The City is the City of London, Britain's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipality is a town or district with local self-government, or the council that runs it.

clue.text: Warned Irish broadcaster involved in corrupt deal

indicators.note: involved in means the broadcaster sits inside the scrambled deal
corrupt suggests the word deal is spoiled, its letters jumbled

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster, Raidió Teilifís Éireann

explanation.surface: An Irish TV network caught up in a dodgy deal is given a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges the deal letters into ALED, and 'involved in' signals the insertion of the broadcaster's initials before the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone is to warn them of danger, so warned and alerted are synonyms.

clue.text: Interference restricting Italian article recalled suppression

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, means the whole construction is read in reverse
restricting means the interference word holds the article inside it

parts.note: noise is interference on a signal
il is the Italian masculine definite article, the

explanation.surface: Signal interference containing an Italian broadcast was remembered as a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' gives NOISILE, which 'recalled' (called back) then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the omission of a sound or syllable in speech, a suppression of part of a word.

clue.text: Solitary fellow avoids being in metropolis

definitions.note: a noun here: a solitary is a person who lives alone

indicators.note: avoids means the fellow word is kept out, removed from the resident word

parts.note: a Londoner is someone living in London, the British metropolis
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A lonely man keeps out of the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solitary fellow' tempts as the definition, but 'fellow' is DON, which 'avoids' removes from LONDONER, a person in the metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is a recluse: someone who prefers to be alone, just like a loner.

clue.text: Going round Pimlico drinking vermouth is unwise

indicators.note: drinking means the scrambled district takes the vermouth inside it
going round suggests the district's letters are turned about into a new arrangement

parts.note: it is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Touring a smart London district while sipping vermouth is a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Pimlico is a district of central London. 'Going round' rearranges it into IMPOLIC, and 'drinking' signals the insertion. Gin and it is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolitic actions are imprudent or tactless, failing to serve one's own interests.

clue.text: China shelled military personnel occupying flat

indicators.note: occupying means the shelled forces sit inside the flat word, as troops occupy ground

parts.note: a plain is a flat stretch of land

indicators.note: shelled means the outer letters are stripped off like a shell

parts.note: the forces are military personnel

explanation.surface: A country bombarded troops encamped on low-lying ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country and 'shelled' like bombardment; shelling here strips the outer letters, leaving ORCE, which 'occupying' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine ceramic ware, and porcelain is the translucent material it is made from.

clue.text: Hack left books appearing retrospectively in Southern Herald

indicators.note: in means the reversed pieces are placed within the herald word

parts.note: a town crier was a herald making public announcements

indicators.note: retrospectively, looking backwards, means these pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A journalist quit, with his books turning up in an old copy of the Southern Herald newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' turns L and BB into BBL, which goes 'in' CRIER; S comes first. 'Southern Herald' reads as a newspaper title.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a poor-quality writer, and a scribbler is a dismissive term for the same kind of author.

clue.text: Succeed on location

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a place is a location

explanation.surface: Achieve success at the site itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' means do well on the surface but follow on from someone here.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to follow them in a post, which is to replace them.

clue.text: Rescue has trouble stopping attack

indicators.note: stopping means the trouble word plugs the attack word, like a stopper inside it

parts.note: a bout is an attack, as of illness
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: An emergency rescue runs into difficulty halting an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailout is a financial rescue, as when a government props up a failing bank.

clue.text: Plant beginning to open by entrance to orifice

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of open is taken

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in two by four
a lip is the rim at the opening of a cavity or orifice

explanation.surface: A flower starts opening beside the mouth of a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flowering plant of the primrose family, a relative of the cowslip.

clue.text: Appearing in court under testing conditions?

definitions.meaning: a defendant appearing before a court
a product or scheme being tried out is ..., the question mark flagging the pun

explanation.surface: Someone standing in the dock under stressful circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: On trial means both facing judgement in court and being tested on a provisional basis.

clue.text: Suspect nearly caught stealing

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A suspect was almost arrested for theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, the taking of someone else's property.

clue.text: Suggests naughty child is untruthful

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to be untruthful is to lie, so it lies

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a mischievous youngster is telling fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to suggest it indirectly without stating it outright.

clue.text: Hair-rising feature of fiscal policy

indicators.note: of means the answer is a part taken out of the following words, a piece of them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hair-raising aspect of tax policy, with a pun on hair rising.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Hair-rising' as the definition, but an adjective cannot stand for the noun SCALP; 'Hair-rising feature', the part of the head hair grows from, does, leaving 'of' to signal the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The scalp is the skin on top of the head, the body part from which hair grows.

clue.text: Tehran bombed close to school entrance

indicators.note: bombed means the city's letters are blown apart and reassembled
close to means the final letter of school is taken

explanation.surface: Iran's capital is attacked near the gates of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a noun, a doorway, but is the verb, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or fill them with wonder, the same as to enthral.

clue.text: Husked bran sticks together around cereal

indicators.note: sticks means the husked bran is lodged inside the turned word
around, turned about, means the word along is read backwards

parts.note: along means together, as in along with

indicators.note: husked means the outer letters of bran are stripped away like a husk

explanation.surface: Bran with its husks off clumps together round some breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives GNOLA, and 'sticks' lodges the husked bran after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola is a breakfast food of baked oats, nuts and dried fruit, a type of cereal.

clue.text: Soldier eating fruit for nourishment

indicators.note: eating means the soldier takes the fruit inside

parts.note: a soldier is a kind of ant, the caste that defends the colony
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A soldier eats a piece of fruit to keep himself going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests a military abbreviation, but it is ANT, a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or sustenance, anything that nourishes.

clue.text: Ultimately, what wouldn't be wanted by criminal at the end, aptly

definitions.text: Ultimately, what wouldn't be wanted by criminal at the end, aptly

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are disordered, rearranged unlawfully
ultimately means the last letter of what is taken, the one that wouldn't be wanted

explanation.surface: The final punishment, aptly enough, is the last thing a criminal wants at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: AT THE END APTLY has one T too many: 'wouldn't be wanted' removes the last letter of 'what', and the rest is rearranged. Read whole, the clue describes capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The death penalty is execution as punishment, the very end no criminal would want.
